title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26) that measures how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; see Methods for a verified deviation from the preregistered ensemble) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Provider call failures reduced the effective sample (28 failed hosted model calls recorded). We release a complete artifact bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json lists SHA‑256s for every per‑episode file) so every reported number is traceable to immutable files. We document the verified deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed) and discuss operational lessons for measuring and engineering defended agentic NetOps workflows.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM pipelines that translate natural‑language intent into network configuration changes promise automation gains for NetOps but also create a concrete safety problem: fluent natural‑language outputs may produce configuration changes that are syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe (policy‑violating or availability‑reducing) when executed. Prior work proposes layered defenses—deterministic verification (reachability/policy checks), generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating—but published evaluations commonly lack preregistration, paired causal designs, and artifact‑anchored reproducibility. We preregistered hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 to (1) quantify an empirical claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate for intent→configuration tasks in a deterministic simulator, and (2) measure whether a preregistered guarded defense reduces that rate versus an unguarded baseline. All model calls, validator traces, per‑episode scoring decisions, and analysis artifacts were archived with SHA‑256 checksums. We report the preregistered confirmatory analysis, document a verified execution deviation that changed the defended pipeline that actually ran, present conservative sensitivity accounting for failed provider calls, and discuss operational implications for deploying defended agentic NetOps.
sections.related_work: Relevant literatures include: deterministic formal verification of network configurations (NetKAT/SMT and header‑space analyses) that provide operational validators; LLM‑for‑NetOps and tool‑augmented agent research advocating generate–validate–repair patterns and constraint injection; and recent taxonomies of agentic failure modes that motivate conservative gating. Surveys and artifactized case studies of tool‑augmented agents and RAG pipelines stress traceability and verifier‑assisted generation. Our work differs by preregistering a paired confirmatory measurement, archiving full per‑call and per‑episode artifacts (responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis files), and publishing exact artifact hashes to permit deterministic reproduction of every reported number.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design with N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in safe‑execution rates). Analysis plan: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes and paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Execution contract. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini"). Planned guarded pipeline: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. Preregistered retry and missingness rules were frozen prior to execution; the manifest of the frozen preregistration is archived. Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks with explicit initial states, required safe sequences, and operational constraints; per‑task payloads and reference answers are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (example task payloads and reference answers are included in the run archive). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated configuration text, executes commands in an isolated deterministic simulator, computes final state, and returns a binary safe/unsafe decision together with rich validator_trace (validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, violation_codes). All per‑episode scoring JSONs include the validator_trace and are archived at execution/scoring/*.json (SHA‑256s listed in execution/execution_manifest.json). Execution, retries, and logging. The execution manifest records every model call, provider trace, and per‑episode artifact with SHA‑256s (execution/execution_manifest.json). Planned maximum_model_calls=600 and a single deterministic retry policy for failed provider calls; failures and provider call audit information were archived for reproducible sensitivity analyses. Deviation auditing. The runtime included an audit that records stage_counts and condition_counts (execution/execution_manifest.json). The manifest shows stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts {"shared":300, "guarded":1}, which documents a verified execution deviation: the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble did not execute; the guarded condition archived therefore corresponds to a deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation (not the preregistered ensemble). Missingness and sensitivity. The preregistration defined the primary analysis on complete pairs and a conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe. We follow that plan and archive all missingness files (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) and provider_call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json) so readers can audit how failed calls affect inference.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json; artifact SHA‑256s are listed inside that manifest). Provider call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. Complete analyzable pairs for the primary confirmatory test = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA‑256 archived). Primary paired analysis (complete pairs). The paired contingency on the 272 complete pairs is: n11=271 (safe in both baseline and guarded), n10=1 (safe baseline & unsafe guarded), n01=0 (unsafe baseline & safe guarded), n00=0 (unsafe both) (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Interpretation: the discordant counts (n10=1, n01=0) yield an exact McNemar p = 1.0, i.e., the paired test provides no evidence for a difference on the analyzable pairs; the observed absolute difference is numerically small. Missingness and conservative sensitivity. Missingness summary: complete_pairs = 272; both_missing_pairs = 28; failed_baseline_episodes = 28; failed_guarded_episodes = 28 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Applying the preregistered conservative sensitivity (treat failed episodes as unsafe) to the full planned N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. The sensitivity result is reported to bound conclusions under provider failures. Representative artifacts. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs and raw responses are archived; example artifact paths and SHA‑256s include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256:465d73fd...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256:b227731a...), and execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256:8f38c8be...). These files contain the normalized candidate configuration, the validator_trace, and the scoring decision used in the primary analysis. Reproducibility. The minimal artifact set to reproduce the primary analysis is: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json (all paths and SHA‑256s are present in the run archive). The full per‑call provider traces and scoring JSONs permit deterministic re‑derivation of every reported statistic.
sections.discussion: Main empirical takeaways. (1) On the 272 analyzable pairs the deployed validator + simulated human gate applied to single shared LLM generations yielded near‑perfect acceptance (baseline safe ≈ 99.6%, guarded safe = 100%), but the observed paired improvement is extremely small (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive on the completed pairs (exact McNemar p = 1.0). (2) A verified, artifact‑backed execution deviation prevented testing the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble: the archived guarded condition corresponds to validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation, not the intended ensemble. (3) Provider call failures materially reduced effective N: execution/execution_manifest.json records failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. These failures limit the study's power to detect small absolute defenses effects and highlight an operational fragility in measured agentic pipelines.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired measurement of LLM→action safety with full artifact archiving. On 272 complete pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (paired absolute increase = 0.003676470588235281; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0000,0.0110294]; McNemar p = 1.0). Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the realized sample and a verified deviation prevented testing the preregistered consensus ensemble. All per‑episode raw responses, provider call traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums (execution/execution_manifest.json lists them) so every reported number is reproducible from the stored files. We recommend re‑execution with robust provider‑call orchestration and a seeded, archived consensus stage so the preregistered ensemble hypothesis can be tested with sufficient effective N. The archived bundle documents both the measured near‑perfect validator acceptance on analyzable pairs and the operational failure modes that must be mitigated before ensemble defenses can be reliably evaluated in practice.

limitations: Single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
